slides.texte_overlay:
Things you should stop doing
on a first date
Stop checking your phone at the table. Not once, not "just quickly." Put it away before you sit down. She'll remember the guy who gave her his full attention, not the one checking football scores.
Stop turning it into a job interview. "What do you do? Where are you from? Siblings?" Ask one real question and follow it. A date is a conversation, not a form you're filling in together.
Stop talking about your ex. Not the drama, not the lessons, not the funny story. It makes her wonder if you're over it, and it takes the focus off the two of you sitting right there.
Stop being rude to the waiter. Thank them, be patient, tip well. She's watching how you treat people who can't do anything for you, and that one moment tells her more than an hour of talking.
Stop running out of things to say. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you will always have a good story ready. Interesting people are easy, and fun, to date.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: awkward silences and the same three questions. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app, and you've always got a good story to share. Easy.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop pretending to be someone you're not. Fake hobbies, fake confidence, fake opinions. If it works, you'll have to keep pretending. Be the real version and see if she likes that guy.
Stop letting her get home without checking in. "Text me when you're home safe." It's small, it's kind, and it's exactly what a decent guy does at the end of a first date.
